figures.caption: Table 1. OLS regression coefficients predicting tract-level asthma prevalence from proximity to hazardous waste facilities and socioeconomic/demographic context (standardized predictors; HC1 robust SEs).
Model fit statistics for the global OLS model (robust standard errors).
Variance inflation factors (VIF) for main-effect covariates used in OLS/GWR (excluding interactions).
Global Moran's I for asthma prevalence and for OLS residuals (Queen contiguity, row-standardized).
Stratified mean differences in asthma prevalence (within 3 km vs outside) by terciles of poverty, Black population share, and median income.
Choropleth of tract-level asthma prevalence overlaid with hazardous waste facility locations across North Carolina.
Distance to the nearest hazardous waste facility (from tract centroids), mapped by tract across North Carolina.
Local Moran's I (LISA) cluster map identifying significant hot spots/cold spots of asthma prevalence (Queen contiguity, p ≤ 0.05).
Geographically weighted regression (GWR) map of the spatially varying association between hazardous-waste proximity (ln distance) and asthma prevalence.
Local R² from the GWR model, highlighting where hazardous-waste proximity and covariates better explain asthma prevalence.
Scatter of tract asthma prevalence versus hazardous-waste proximity (ln distance), stratified by poverty terciles to illustrate contextual variation.
Table 2. Stratified OLS estimates of the proximity (ln distance) association with asthma prevalence across socioeconomic/demographic context (median splits; standardized predictors; HC1 robust SEs).
Choropleth map of asthma prevalence across North Carolina census tracts.
Choropleth map of tract centroid distance to the nearest hazardous waste facility (km).
Scatterplot of tract-level asthma prevalence versus distance to nearest hazardous waste facility, with binned mean trend.
Table 3. Key quantitative results: proximity effect estimates, interaction significance, and spatial autocorrelation diagnostics.
